recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-6041 unless a future work-group issue reopens the broader Timing open-range design.
issue_request: FHIR-6041 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core datatypes request raised against DSTU1 because Timing.repeat had an invariant saying durationMax requires duration, but the Repeat element did not define durationMax. The approved resolution was to add durationMax.
initial_application: Git commit 9280e1ab4eb7f8721beb0a9a8843e958c8d8240e, converted from SVN revision 5610, is titled "#6041 - add durationMax" and added the Timing.repeat.durationMax row to source/datatypes/timing.xml. This matches the Jira application comment citing SVN revision 5610.
additional_context: Timing is listed as an active datatype in source/fhir.ini, marked normative, and assigned the tim abbreviation, so source/datatypes/timing.xml is current build-scope source. Later Timing issues FHIR-8734 and FHIR-16986 changed nearby range wording but did not remove durationMax; FHIR-16986 is already represented on the combined branch. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later core decision that conflicts with the current durationMax model.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source defines Timing.repeat.durationMax as 0..1 decimal, describes it as the paired duration range upper value, and retains the invariant requiring duration when durationMax is present.
